title: Compile once, cache forever
prompt: Implement `static Func<int, bool> CachedCheck(int threshold)` that compiles the predicate `x => x >= threshold && x % 2 == 0` for the given threshold and caches the delegate in a static ConcurrentDictionary<int, Func<int, bool>>. The test proves compilation happens once: the SECOND call with the same threshold must return the SAME delegate instance (ReferenceEquals), invoking the cached delegate allocates nothing, and the boundary is exact — CachedCheck(10) accepts 10.

tests.name: same-instance
tests.hint: GetOrAdd on a static ConcurrentDictionary; build + compile only inside the factory.

tests.name: no-alloc-per-call
tests.hint: After caching, invoking is a plain delegate call — zero allocations.
